The failing test `testReadWinZipArchive` tries to read a WinZip archive using `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipFile`. The test opens the zip file, reads some entries, and then ensures that the entries can be read successfully before closing the zip file.

The current bug report states that when trying to extract a zip file created with WinZip containing Unicode extra fields using `ZipFile`, `ZipFile.getInputStream()` returns null for entries that were previously retrieved with `ZipFile.getEntry()`. This indicates that there might be an issue with handling Unicode extra fields in the `ZipFile` class.

Looking at the `ZipFile` constructor, particularly the constructor that takes a `File`, encoding, and a boolean flag for using Unicode extra fields, we can see that it initializes the `useUnicodeExtraFields` field based on the input parameter. This parameter controls whether Unicode extra fields should be used.

The `closeQuietly` method of `ZipFile` is responsible for closing the zip file. It simply calls the `close` method on the `ZipFile` instance, handling any `IOException` by ignoring it.

To diagnose the issue further, we need to inspect how Unicode extra fields are handled in the `ZipFile` class and ensure that they are correctly processed when reading the entries from the WinZip archive.

Next, I will provide the methods that would be the best locations to be fixed based on this diagnosis.
```
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipFile.ZipFile(java.io.File, java.lang.String, boolean)
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipFile.closeQuietly(org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipFile)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
